anomaly_def.Name: Replication Synchronization Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Standbys or downstream consumers cannot receive, store, or replay transaction-log records as fast as the primary generates them, causing sustained replication lag.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Allocated disk or logical free space for datafiles, logs, archives, temp areas, or backups is exhausted, leading to allocation failures and stalled database operations.

Composite definition: Both anomalies manifest concurrently—the replication pipeline is backlogged while one or more nodes (primary or replicas) are simultaneously running out of space needed to write or retain log and data blocks.

Combined phenomena: 1) Rapidly widening replication-position gaps alongside shrinking free space on primary and/or replica volumes. 2) Retained WAL/redo or relay-log files piling up because they cannot be recycled until replicas catch up, hastening space exhaustion on the primary. 3) On replicas, full disks prevent new relay logs from being written, which in turn halts apply threads and pushes lag even higher. 4) Error messages such as "no space left on device," "cannot allocate WAL segment," or "replication receiver stalled" appear together, and failover readiness metrics degrade sharply. 5) User transactions may start failing when the primary can no longer allocate new log segments or when temporary-space shortages collide with long-running queries.

Causal chain: Replication lag forces the primary to retain extra log segments; these retained files consume space that would normally be reclaimed, accelerating space depletion. Once storage reaches critical thresholds, archive, backup, or checkpoint processes fail, further preventing log recycling and deepening the lag. Conversely, initial space pressure on a replica (e.g., from unchecked data growth or oversized temp usage) can block the writing of incoming relay logs, which stalls replay and propagates back to the primary, increasing file retention there. The two root causes thus reinforce each other in a feedback loop that escalates from mild lag or moderate disk usage into a compound failure affecting durability, availability, and recovery objectives.

entry.official_definition: Controls how long STOP REPLICA waits before timing out.
entry.trigger_condition: A STOP REPLICA administrative operation waits longer than rpl_stop_replica_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The administrative replication stop operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when replication endpoints stop exchanging or applying data within the configured timeout window, causing the channel to be considered inactive.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver status, upstream and downstream connectivity, and whether lag or stalled apply is preventing timely progress.
